lines.text: A floor has a ring of blue tiles around the edge and white tiles inside.
lines.caption: A floor has a ring of blue tiles around the edge and white tiles inside.

lines.text: Just from two counts, can we find its shape? Let's see!
lines.caption: Just from two counts, can we find its shape? Let's see!

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's tile this one together.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's tile this one together.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: A rectangular floor is covered with square tiles, each one foot on a side.
lines.caption: A rectangular floor is covered with square tiles, each one foot on a side.

lines.text: The forty tiles along the edge are blue.
lines.caption: The forty tiles along the edge are blue.

lines.text: The other eighty tiles are white.
lines.caption: The other eighty tiles are white.

lines.text: How many feet longer is the floor than it is wide?
lines.caption: How many feet longer is the floor than it is wide?

lines.text: Here are the five choices.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices.

lines.text: Forty blue plus eighty white makes one hundred twenty tiles in all.
lines.caption: Forty blue plus eighty white makes one hundred twenty tiles in all.

lines.text: Each tile is one foot, so the floor's length times its width is one hundred twenty.
lines.caption: Each tile is one foot, so the floor's length times its width is one hundred twenty.

lines.text: We want the difference: length minus width.
lines.caption: We want the difference: length minus width.

lines.text: Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's make a list of floors with one hundred twenty tiles, and count each one's edge.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's make a list of floors with one hundred twenty tiles, and count each one's edge.

lines.text: First, how do we count edge tiles? Take the whole top row and the whole bottom row.
lines.caption: First, how do we count edge tiles? Take the whole top row and the whole bottom row.

lines.text: Then add the two side columns, but skip their corners. Five minus two leaves three each.
lines.caption: Then add the two side columns, but skip their corners. Five minus two leaves three each.

lines.text: On this small example, that's seven plus seven plus three plus three, twenty edge tiles.
lines.caption: On this small example, that's seven plus seven plus three plus three, twenty edge tiles.

lines.text: Long, thin floors are almost all edge.
lines.caption: Long, thin floors are almost all edge.

lines.text: Sixty by two has one hundred twenty edge tiles. Forty by three has eighty-two.
lines.caption: Sixty by two has one hundred twenty edge tiles. Forty by three has eighty-two.

lines.text: As the floor gets squarer, the edge shrinks: sixty-four, fifty-four, forty-eight.
lines.caption: As the floor gets squarer, the edge shrinks: sixty-four, fifty-four, forty-eight.

lines.text: Fifteen by eight gives forty-two. So close!
lines.caption: Fifteen by eight gives forty-two. So close!

lines.text: Twelve by ten gives exactly forty. And the inside is ten by eight, eighty white tiles. Perfect!
lines.caption: Twelve by ten gives exactly forty. And the inside is ten by eight, eighty white tiles. Perfect!

lines.text: Twelve minus ten is two. The floor is two feet longer. That's Choice B!
lines.caption: Twelve minus ten is two. The floor is two feet longer. That's Choice B!

scenes.chapter: Solution 2: the edge gives a sum

lines.text: Here's a faster way.
lines.caption: Here's a faster way.

lines.text: The edge is two lengths plus two widths, minus the four corners we'd count twice.
lines.caption: The edge is two lengths plus two widths, minus the four corners we'd count twice.

lines.text: So two lengths plus two widths, minus four, is forty.
lines.caption: So two lengths plus two widths, minus four, is forty.

lines.text: Add four: two lengths plus two widths is forty-four. So length plus width is twenty-two.
lines.caption: Add four: two lengths plus two widths is forty-four. So length plus width is twenty-two.

lines.text: Now find two numbers that add to twenty-two and multiply to one hundred twenty.
lines.caption: Now find two numbers that add to twenty-two and multiply to one hundred twenty.

lines.text: Eleven times eleven is one hundred twenty-one, just one too many.
lines.caption: Eleven times eleven is one hundred twenty-one, just one too many.

lines.text: Spread them apart by one each: twelve and ten.
lines.caption: Spread them apart by one each: twelve and ten.

lines.text: Twelve times ten is one hundred twenty. Again, a difference of two!
lines.caption: Twelve times ten is one hundred twenty. Again, a difference of two!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? When you know a sum and a product. That pins down the two numbers.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? When you know a sum and a product. That pins down the two numbers.

lines.text: Now let's test every choice. We know length plus width is twenty-two.
lines.caption: Now let's test every choice. We know length plus width is twenty-two.

lines.text: A difference of one or three can't work.
lines.caption: A difference of one or three can't work.

lines.text: Twenty-two minus an odd number is odd, and half of an odd number isn't whole.
lines.caption: Twenty-two minus an odd number is odd, and half of an odd number isn't whole.

lines.text: A difference of four gives nine and thirteen. That's one hundred seventeen tiles, three short.
lines.caption: A difference of four gives nine and thirteen. That's one hundred seventeen tiles, three short.

lines.text: A difference of six gives eight and fourteen. That's only one hundred twelve tiles.
lines.caption: A difference of six gives eight and fourteen. That's only one hundred twelve tiles.

lines.text: Only a difference of two gives ten and twelve, exactly one hundred twenty tiles.
lines.caption: Only a difference of two gives ten and twelve, exactly one hundred twenty tiles.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge?
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge?

lines.text: A new floor has thirty-six blue tiles on the edge and sixty white tiles inside.
lines.caption: A new floor has thirty-six blue tiles on the edge and sixty white tiles inside.

lines.text: How many feet longer is it than it is wide?
lines.caption: How many feet longer is it than it is wide?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. Thirty-six plus sixty is ninety-six tiles in all.
lines.caption: Let's check. Thirty-six plus sixty is ninety-six tiles in all.

lines.text: Add the four corners to thirty-six. Then cut forty in half. Length plus width is twenty.
lines.caption: Add the four corners to thirty-six. Then cut forty in half. Length plus width is twenty.

lines.text: Ten times ten is one hundred, too many. Twelve times eight is ninety-six. That's it!
lines.caption: Ten times ten is one hundred, too many. Twelve times eight is ninety-six. That's it!

lines.text: The inside is ten by six, sixty white tiles. It checks out.
lines.caption: The inside is ten by six, sixty white tiles. It checks out.

lines.text: Twelve minus eight is four. The floor is four feet longer!
lines.caption: Twelve minus eight is four. The floor is four feet longer!

lines.text: If you got four, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you got four, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: Add four to the edge tiles, then cut it in half. That's length plus width.
lines.caption: Add four to the edge tiles, then cut it in half. That's length plus width.

lines.text: Count every tile in the floor to get length times width.
lines.caption: Count every tile in the floor to get length times width.

lines.text: Then find the pair of numbers that fits both.
lines.caption: Then find the pair of numbers that fits both.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep counting, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep counting, and I'll see you next time!
